creator: Dan McCreary

historical periods
Eastern Mediterranean
chronology
BCE and CE dating
dublinCore.description: A to-scale vis-timeline of the nine periods of Eastern Mediterranean history, from the Bronze Age (c. 3200 BCE) to the modern era (2026 CE). Periods only: learners answer six proportion questions before the relevant bands are highlighted and their lengths shown, then click any band to read its dates and the sites on the route from that period. Events are in the appendix companion, eastern-med-events-timeline.

learningObjectives: Compare the order and length of the nine periods of Eastern Mediterranean history by answering six proportion questions before the answers are revealed, scoring at least 5 of 6

controls.label: Answer choices
controls.description: Commit one answer per question; one attempt each

controls.label: Next
controls.description: Go to the next question and return to the full span

controls.label: Restart
controls.description: Clear the score and return to question 1

visualElements.description: Nine colored period bands drawn to scale in three staggered rows, with faint full-height shading
Question, feedback with the reason, running score, and an infobox for the selected band with its sites on the route

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, then check against a to-scale display
keyQuestions: Which lasted longer: the Bronze Age or the Classical period?
About how much of the whole timeline does the Bronze Age fill?
Which lasted longer: the Byzantine period or the Ottoman period?
Which lasted longer: the Classical, Hellenistic, and Roman periods together, or the Byzantine period alone?
How many years is the Roman period, 31 BCE to 330 CE?
In which period was writing almost unknown in Greece?
commonMisconceptions: The Classical period was long because it is famous
The Byzantine period was a short epilogue to Rome
Spans across the BCE/CE line are found by subtracting the two numbers
Writing in Greece was continuous from the Bronze Age onward
assessmentOpportunities: Six multiple-choice questions, one attempt each; mastery is 5 of 6 on the first attempt
